newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee ends up as banks go low on dlrs.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee ends up as banks go low on dlrs.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed up in volatile trade on Friday as banks remained low on dollars, believing that short-term depreciation of the local currency has ended and lack of commercial demand, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 58.48 to the dollar, after opening at 58.58, rising to 58.37 and falling to 58.70, they said.
"The rupee gained in volatile trade as speculators tried to minimise losses as they unloaded dollars," said a Sampath Bank dealer.

Banks, which had dollars due to the belief that depreciation of the rupee would continue and a lack of imports, began selling the currency earlier this week after the Central Bank turned indifferent to the greenback.
Some said the dollar was also falling due to excess supply caused by big inward remittances.
"Foreign funds have been coming into the share market and about 15 million dollars is said to have come as compensation for Gulf War victims," said a Seylan Bank dealer.
Overnight call money rates closed at 15 percent after rising to 16 and falling to 14, dealers said.
